claims.text: High-temperature irradiation near the order-disorder transition induces ballistic mixing in high-entropy nanoalloys.
Ballistic mixing disrupts short-range order and grain-boundary elemental segregation.
Disruption of short-range order and segregation suppresses precipitation and promotes a refined, chemically homogeneous grain structure.
A refined, homogeneous grain structure enhances structural and chemical stability.
W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf can be prepared as thin and thick refractory high-entropy-alloy films with nanometer-scale grains.
Annealing the W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf film at 1173 K produces grain growth.
Annealing alone causes Hf segregation to grain boundaries in the W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf nanoalloy.
The alloy can be exposed to combined He+ and Kr+ irradiation to approximately 8.5 dpa and 9% He at high temperature.
Dual-beam He+ and Kr+ irradiation is conducted throughout the stated 1073-1173 K range.
The cited experiments include an annealing condition and an irradiation condition at 1173 K.
High-energy recoil events create cascade substructures that enforce ballistic mixing.
Ballistic mixing homogenizes the chemical distribution by reducing Hf segregation.
Disruption of short-range order prevents nucleation of harmful precipitates.
Compared with annealing alone, irradiation produces grain refinement rather than grain growth.
Compared with annealing alone, irradiation diminishes or eliminates Hf enrichment at grain boundaries.
No precipitation will be detectable after irradiation.
Annealing-only samples show moderate grain coarsening.
Annealing-only samples show grain-boundary Hf segregation, and related quaternary alloys have a propensity for precipitation.
The proposed mechanism applies near the alloy's order-disorder transition temperature.
Temperatures substantially below or above this range, or markedly different dose rates, may produce thermal-diffusion-dominated or non-ballistic structural evolution.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that the only differing variable is the presence of irradiation-induced ballistic events, but the irradiated group also receives implanted He and Kr-ion exposure. Thus the comparison does not isolate ballistic mixing from implanted-gas or ion-species effects.
